trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going up would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
Going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
Going right would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes down.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to number 3 would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going right would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So my guess (left from number 2) was wrong, so the line must go down.
Going right would leave both cell (6,8) and cell (8,8) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going down would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (7,4). So the line goes left.
I can't rule out up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.

Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.

Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.

Going up would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (1,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
